claims.text: Replacing part of a conventional refractory high-entropy alloy with low-activation refractory elements will increase its compositional complexity.
Increasing compositional complexity through low-activation alloying will improve radiation tolerance.
The proposed compositional modification will preserve mechanical integrity.
Increasing compositional complexity will enhance lattice distortion.
Increasing compositional complexity will enhance local chemical ordering.
Introducing low-activation elements will increase lattice distortion.
Increased lattice distortion will suppress irradiation-induced defect mobility.
Increased lattice distortion will suppress irradiation-induced defect clustering.
Suppressed defect mobility and clustering will reduce the accumulation of voids and dislocation loops.
Reduced accumulation of irradiation-induced defects will maintain mechanical strength.
Under irradiation, the modified alloy will have a statistically significant lower defect density than the unmodified baseline.
Under irradiation, the modified alloy will exhibit less swelling than the unmodified baseline.
The irradiated modified alloy will retain yield strength and hardness comparable to those of the unmodified baseline.
Temperatures of 600–1000°C and high neutron or plasma flux are representative of fusion-reactor plasma-facing conditions.
The beneficial effect may diminish at irradiation doses or temperatures outside the proposed fusion-relevant range.
